articles.title: Claude Code said "Done." My tests said otherwise. Here's the 20-line fix.
articles.excerpt: If you use Claude Code, you've seen this: claude: Done! Partial refunds are implemented. ✅ Then you run the tests yourself and four of them fail. Claude isn't lying. It stops when the work looks done,…
articles.body: If you use Claude Code, you've seen this: claude: Done! Partial refunds are implemented. ✅ Then you run the tests yourself and four of them fail. Claude isn't lying. It stops when the work looks done, because it has no other signal. If nothing tells it the tests are red, "looks done" is all it has. So you become the test runner: you check, paste the errors back, wait, and check again. This post shows how to make Claude run that check itself, every time, before it's allowed to say it's finished. Why this is the highest-leverage fix Anthropic's best practices for Claude Code put this first: give Claude a way to verify its work, such as tests, a build, a linter or a script, anything that returns pass or fail.
articles.author: elijahmanlockedin112

articles.title: AI Cloned My Voice From a 3-Second Video. Here Is What My Parent Almost Did With It.
articles.excerpt: ` AI Cloned My Voice From a 3-Second Video. Here Is What My Parent Almost Did With It. This is not a hypothetical. A scammer lifted 15 seconds of audio from a family video posted on social media, ran…
articles.body: ` AI Cloned My Voice From a 3-Second Video. Here Is What My Parent Almost Did With It. This is not a hypothetical. A scammer lifted 15 seconds of audio from a family video posted on social media, ran it through a voice cloning tool, and called an elderly parent claiming to be their child in an emergency. The voice was exact. The panic was convincing. The money was almost sent. The FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report recorded 352 million dollars in losses from adults over 60 tied to AI voice cloning scams. A McAfee survey found 77 percent of people who received a cloned voice call lost money. Average loss: between 500 and 15,000 dollars per victim. This is a developer community. We understand how this technology works better than most people do.

articles.title: Your link previews are blank because og:image is missing. Here is a stdlib-only Python fix
articles.excerpt: When you paste a link to your product, docs page or side project into Slack, Discord, X or LinkedIn, the platform builds a preview card from your page's Open Graph tags. If og:image is missing or poin…
articles.body: When you paste a link to your product, docs page or side project into Slack, Discord, X or LinkedIn, the platform builds a preview card from your page's Open Graph tags. If og:image is missing or points at a generic platform default, the preview is a grey box or a stock logo. That hurts clicks, and you usually don't notice because you never see your own link the way other people do. This post covers three things: A 10-second check for whether your pages have this problem A PNG generator in pure Python (standard library only: no Pillow, no ImageMagick) that makes a 1280x720 cover image How to wire the image into your page 1. Check your og:image in 10 seconds curl -s https://your-site.example/page | grep -io '<meta[^>]*og:image[^>]*>' Three things can come back: Nothing.

articles.body: Originally published on anton.qa . A browser can report dark mode while the page stays white. Checking the setting alone would miss that broken page. The result we want The practice page has a card and an animated notice. Its styling rules should respond to two browser preferences: Dark mode: use the expected dark background, light text and lighter border. Reduced motion: make the notice's visual change immediate. These are requirements for this example.

articles.title: Three timestamp bugs worth catching before they reach your API
articles.excerpt: A timestamp can be a perfectly valid number and still produce the wrong date. The useful questions are: what unit does it use, how is it displayed, and what precision must survive the conversion? Here…
articles.body: A timestamp can be a perfectly valid number and still produce the wrong date. The useful questions are: what unit does it use, how is it displayed, and what precision must survive the conversion? Here are three small checks you can reproduce in JavaScript. The examples use Date because it is common in existing API integrations. 1. Passing Unix seconds to a millisecond constructor Start with this value: const unixSeconds = 1711972800 ; console . log ( new Date ( unixSeconds ). toISOString ()); // 1970-01-20T19:32:52.800Z console . log ( new Date ( unixSeconds * 1000 ). toISOString ()); // 2024-04-01T12:00:00.000Z JavaScript's numeric Date constructor expects milliseconds. Both calls produce valid dates, so an Invalid Date check alone will not catch the first mistake.

The ASCENT (Advanced Spacecraft Energetic Non-Toxic) Propulsion Dual Mode mission is a flight demonstration of a spacecraft about the size of a large shoebox. articles.title: Hubble Spots Chaotic Secret in Galaxy
articles.excerpt: A chaotic secret hides within this seemingly serene image of spiral galaxy NGC 4698 taken by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and released on Sept. 18, 2026. As a spiral galaxy like our own Milky Way gal…
articles.body: ESA/Hubble & NASA, D. Thilker, the MAUVE-HST Team A chaotic secret hides within this seemingly serene image of spiral galaxy NGC 4698 taken by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope and released on Sept. 18, 2026. As a spiral galaxy like our own Milky Way galaxy, NGC 4698 has spiral arms that curl around within a thin disk of stars, gas, and dust. These arms are marked by opaque clumps of brown dust and dotted with small collections of bright blue stars. Unlike many other spiral galaxies, NGC 4698’s delicate spiral arms are only prominent in the outer reaches of the disk; spiral arms often wind down to the very center of a galaxy, but NGC 4698’s spiral arms appear to shy away from its glowing center. The arms instead hover in a ring-like structure around the perimeter of the galaxy.
